question.text: In square units rounded to the nearest integer, the area of $\triangle ABC$ is
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of a right triangle is \[ \mathcal A = \dfrac 1 2 AC \cdot BC. \]

Notice that relative to the given angle $\angle B,$ we have the length of the opposite side $\overline{AC}$ and need to determine the length of the adjacent side $\overline{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $BC{:}$

\begin{align} \tan(m\angle B) & = \dfrac {AC} {BC} \\[5pt] \tan (70^\circ) & = \dfrac {6} {BC} \\[5pt] BC\cdot\tan (70^\circ) & = 6\\[5pt] BC &= \dfrac{6}{\tan (70^{\circ})} \\[5pt] BC &=2.183\ldots \end{align}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is \begin{align} \mathcal A & = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 6 \cdot (2.183\ldots) \\[5pt] &= 6.551\ldots \\[5pt] & \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{7}, \end{align} rounded to the nearest integer.

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Area of a Triangle by Solving for a Variable Given a Trigonometric Ratio of One Angle

question.text: Given that $\tan(m\angle{A}) = 5,$ calculate the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown above.
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC. \]

We are given that $\tan(m\angle{A}) = 5.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{A},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$ \begin{align} \tan(m\angle{A}) &= \dfrac{BC}{AC} \\[5pt] 5 &= \dfrac{2x+4}{x-1} \\[5pt] 5(x-1) &= 2x+4 \\[5pt] 5x-5 &= 2x+4 \\[5pt] 3x &= 9 \\[5pt] x &= 3 \end{align}

So, the side lengths are

\begin{align*} BC &= 2x+4 = 2(3)+4 = 10,\\[5pt] AC &= x-1 = 3-1 = 2. \end{align*}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is \begin{align} \mathcal A & = \dfrac 1 2 AC\cdot BC \\[5pt] &= \dfrac 1 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 10 \\[5pt] &=10. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Area of a Triangle by Solving for a Variable Given a Trigonometric Ratio of One Angle

question.text: Given that $\tan(m\angle{A}) = \dfrac 5 8,$ calculate the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown above.
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC. \]

We are given that $\tan(m\angle{A}) = \dfrac 5 8.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{A},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$

\begin{align} \tan (m\angle{A}) &=\dfrac{BC}{AC} \\[5pt] \dfrac{5}{8} &=\dfrac{3x-2}{4x}\\[5pt] 5(4x) &=8(3x-2)\\[5pt] 20x & = 24x-16\\[5pt] -4x &=-16\\[5pt] x&=4 \end{align}

So, the side lengths are

\begin{align*} BC&=3x-2=3(4)-2=10,\\[5pt] AC&=4x=4(4)=16. \end{align*}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

\begin{align} \mathcal A & = \dfrac 1 2 AC\cdot BC \\[5pt] &= \dfrac 1 2 \cdot 16 \cdot 10 \\[5pt] &= 80. \end{align}

question.text: Given that $\tan \theta = \dfrac{3}{4},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown above.
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC. \]

We are given that $\tan \theta = \dfrac34,$ where $\theta = m\angle{C}.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overline{AC}$ adjacent to $\angle{C}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to find the length of the opposite side $\overline{AB}{:}$

\begin{align} \tan \theta & = \dfrac {AB}{AC}\\[5pt] \dfrac{3}{4}&=\dfrac{AB}{8}\\[5pt] AB & = \dfrac{3}{4} \cdot 8\\[5pt] AB & = 6 \end{align}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

\begin{align} \mathcal A &= \dfrac 1 2 AC \cdot AB \\[5pt] & =\dfrac 1 2 \cdot 8 \cdot 6 \\[5pt] & = 24. \end{align}

question.text: Given that $\tan \theta = \dfrac{4}{5},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown above.
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AB \cdot AC. \]

We are given that $\tan \theta = \dfrac45,$ where $\theta = m\angle{B}.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overline{AB}$ adjacent to $\angle{B}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to find the length of the opposite side $\overline{AC}{:}$

\begin{align} \tan \theta & = \dfrac {AC}{AB}\\[5pt] \dfrac{4}{5}&=\dfrac{AC}{10}\\[5pt] AC & = \dfrac{4}{5} \cdot 10\\[5pt] AC & = 8 \end{align}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

\begin{align} \mathcal A &= \dfrac 1 2 AB \cdot AC \\[5pt] & =\dfrac 1 2 \cdot 10 \cdot 8 \\[5pt] & = 40. \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Area of a Triangle by Solving for a Variable Given an Angle

question.text: Find the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown above.
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AB \cdot BC. \]

We are given that $m\angle{A} = 60^\circ.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{A},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{AB}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$

\begin{align} %\tan{A} &=\dfrac{\textrm{opposite}}{\textrm{adjacent}}\\[5pt] \tan(m\angle{A}) &=\dfrac{BC}{AB}\\[5pt] \tan (60^{\circ}) &= \dfrac{x+2}{\sqrt3\, x}\\[5pt] {\sqrt3} &= \dfrac{x+2}{\sqrt3\, x}\\[5pt] \sqrt3(\sqrt{3}\,x) &= x+2 \\[5pt] 3x &= x+2\\[5pt] 2x &= 2\\[5pt] x &=1 \end{align}

So, the side lengths are \begin{align} BC&= x+2=1 + 2 =3,\\[5pt] AB&=\sqrt3\, x= \sqrt{3}(1) = \sqrt{3}. \end{align}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

\begin{align*} \mathcal A & = \dfrac 1 2 \cdot AB \cdot BC\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \sqrt{3} \cdot 3\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Area of a Triangle by Solving for a Variable Given an Angle

question.text: Find the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown above.
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 BC\cdot AB . \]

We are given that $m\angle{A} = 30^\circ.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{A},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{AB}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$

\begin{align} %\tan{A} &=\dfrac{\textrm{opposite}}{\textrm{adjacent}}\\[5pt] \tan(m\angle{A}) &=\dfrac{BC}{AB}\\[5pt] \tan (30^{\circ}) &= \dfrac{2x}{\sqrt{3}\,x+3}\\[5pt] \dfrac{\sqrt3}{3} &= \dfrac{2x}{\sqrt{3}\,x+3}\\[5pt] \sqrt3(\sqrt{3}\,x+3) &= 3\cdot2x \\[5pt] 3x +3\sqrt3 &= 6x\\[5pt] %3\sqrt3 &= 6x-3x\\[5pt] 3\sqrt3&=3x\\[5pt] x &=\sqrt{3} \end{align}

So, the side lengths are

\begin{align} BC&= 2x = 2\sqrt{3},\\[5pt] AB&= \sqrt{3}\,x+3 =\sqrt{3}\,(\sqrt{3})+3= 6. \end{align}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

\begin{align*} \mathcal A & = \dfrac 1 2 \cdot BC \cdot AB\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot 2\sqrt{3}\cdot 6\\[5pt] &=6\sqrt{3}. \end{align*}

question.text: In square units rounded to one decimal place, the area of $\triangle ABC$ is
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC. \]

We are given that $m\angle{B} = 72^\circ.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{B},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$

\begin{align*} \tan (m\angle{B}) &=\dfrac{AC}{BC} \\[5pt] \tan (72^{\circ}) &=\dfrac{3x+4}{2x-1} \\[5pt] (2x-1)\cdot \tan (72^{\circ}) &= 3x+4 \\[5pt] 2x\cdot \tan (72^{\circ})-\tan (72^{\circ}) &= 3x+4 \\[5pt] {x} (2\tan (72^{\circ})-3) &= 4+ \tan (72^{\circ})\\[5pt] x &= \dfrac{4+ \tan (72^{\circ})}{ 2\tan (72^{\circ})-3} \\[5pt] x &= 2.243\,0\ldots \end{align*}

So, the side lengths are \begin{align*} BC &= 2x -1= 2(2.243\,0\ldots)-1=3.486\,1\ldots, \\[5pt] AC &= 3x+4 = 3(2.243\,0\ldots) +4= 10.729\,1\ldots. \end{align*}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is \begin{align*} \mathcal A %& = \dfrac 1 2 \cdot AC \cdot BC\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}(10.729\,1\ldots)(3.486\,1\ldots) \\[5pt] &= 18.701\,3\ldots \\[5pt] &\approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{18.7}, \end{align*} rounded to one decimal place.
